chapter_theme: Receiving the discus (சக்கரப்பேறு): Vishnu's discus comes from Siva, who made and owns all things; Vishnu could not bear it until he worshipped Siva, who divided its power between Vishnu, Shakti and himself; at Daksha's sacrifice the discus Vishnu hurled at Siva's side was useless.

367.reading: The verse names things the Lord has made and owns: Mal and his gift, ahankara, the elephant, the discus in the sky, the silver mountain, Indra's city Amaravati and the enjoyments of the seven worlds.
367.nuance: The first two lines are hard to parse: மால் போதகன் may be 'Mal the elephant' or 'Mal the one taught', and காங்காரம் is read as ahankara. The last line is clear: he made and possesses all. The verse sets up the chapter by making the discus one of Siva's possessions.

368.reading: Damodara, having received the discus but unable to bear it, worshipped Hara with longing, and the fitting good power was divided into a share for him.
368.nuance: Who makes the share (கூறு செய்தது) is not said; the next verse makes it Siva. The variant திரிக்கவொண்ணாமை (could not spin it) for தரிக்கவொண்ணாமை (could not bear it) changes the difficulty from holding the weapon to wielding it.

369.reading: Intending it in portions, he divided the good discus: a share he gave to Mal, a share he gave to Shakti, and a share he kept and bore as his own form.
369.nuance: கூறது (a share) begins every line. The discus here seems to stand for a power (சக்தி) that can be divided rather than a single weapon; what Shakti's share and Siva's share mean is left unstated.

370.reading: At Daksha's sacrifice, when Damodara loosed his discus at the moon-crowned one among the heroes who shattered the sacrifice, fire was spat out in the hand of Vayu.
370.nuance: The last line (அக்கி உமிழ்ந்தது வாயுக் கரத்திலே) is obscure: it may mean the discus spat fire, or that it was rendered harmless. In one telling Virabhadra's side swallowed the discus. சசிமுடி (moon-crowned) is Siva or Virabhadra.

links.note: 349 says only that Siva gave the discus to Achyuta; 368 and 369 tell how Vishnu could not bear it until he worshipped Siva, who then divided its power.
353 tells of Daksha's sacrifice breaking down at Siva's anger; 370 adds an episode from it, Vishnu turning the discus Siva gave him against Siva's side.

368 says Damodara received the discus and, unable to bear it, worshipped Hara with longing (விருப்புடன் அர்ச்சிக்க). The Thiruppugazh song tells the story behind the gift: Vishnu worshipped with a thousand lotuses a day, offered his eye when one was missing, and was given the ஆழி that cut Jalandhara. Both make Vishnu's discus a gift won by worship of Siva.

369 says Siva divided the discus and gave one share to Mal and one to Shakti (கொடுத்தனன் சத்திக்கு). 1085 shows Parashakti bearing conch and discus (சங்கு சக்கரம்), the weapon usually Vishnu's, which is what 369's sharing would lead one to expect.

source_issues: 368: variant திரிக்கவொண் (spin, wield) for தரிக்கவொண் (bear) changes the sense.
370 line 4 (அக்கி உமிழ்ந்தது வாயுக் கரத்திலே) is obscure and may be corrupt.
